svg.title: The three-way witness rule of coincides, shown with the holiday table national (covering 2026-01-01..2026-07-15) and month windows. The May window holds the holidays 5/3–5/6 as witnesses, so true. The June window has no holiday and lies entirely within the covering, so false. The July window has no holiday and from 7/16 on lies outside the table (an annotated interval), so out-of-coverage. Evaluated over [2026-05-01, 2026-08-01), month |> first |> filter(m => coincides(national, month, m)) returns 2026-05-01, the same with not returns 2026-06-01, and both carry "⚠ out-of-coverage 2026-07-01..2026-08-01 (JP.national covering 2026-01-01..2026-07-15)".
svg.text: The witness rule of coincides: one witness → true; none → false or out-of-coverage
Holiday table national: covering 2026-01-01..2026-07-15 (from 7/16 on, outside the table). Evaluate coincides(national, month, m) over [2026-05-01, 2026-08-01)
A point of S outside any annotated interval (a witness) is in the window → true (5/1 comes out). One witness is enough
No witness; the whole window is inside the effective coverage → false (6/1 is dropped; with not, it comes out)
No witness; part of the window (7/16 on) is outside the table → out-of-coverage (7/1 is dropped; the annotation covers 7/1..8/1 = F75)
holiday or not, the table does not know
month |> first |> filter(m => coincides(national, month, m)) #=> 2026-05-01
month |> first |> filter(m => not coincides(national, month, m)) #=> 2026-06-01
True and false are asymmetric: true is settled by one witness and depends on no unknown data; false depends on the coverage being complete (ADR-38 decision 4).
Out-of-coverage does not turn true under not (7/1 is dropped by both expressions). If unwanted, extend covering to the end of July and it disappears.
